C-VIM-RECORDS-JUMPS.Summary: Add Vim-style first-row navigation to records and establish a project shortcut convention.
C-VIM-RECORDS-JUMPS.Problem: Records supports first-row navigation with Home and last-row navigation with End/G, but does not support the Vim-style gg first-row binding or document a convention for future shortcuts.

Goals.Goal: Support gg to move to the first row in the currently active records panel while preserving ge and gs focus sequences.
Document gg and G as first-row and last-row navigation in the records help.
Set a project rule to prefer familiar Vim-style keyboard shortcuts when adding shortcuts where they fit the interaction.

Constraints.Constraint: Keep the shortcut scoped to records navigation and operate on the active exercises or sets panel.
Preserve existing Home and End row-jump behavior and existing ge/gs panel focus behavior.
Follow Go formatting rules in all changed Go source and test files.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Change paging, dialog input, help dismissal, persistence, or workout data behavior.
Replace existing keyboard shortcuts or introduce configurable key bindings.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: On the exercises panel, gg selects the first exercise; on the sets panel, gg selects the first set. G continues to select the last row in either active panel.
ge and gs remain usable after the g-prefix handling change, and Home/End behavior remains available.
The help view documents first row as home/gg and last row as end/G.
AGENTS.md instructs contributors to prefer familiar Vim-style bindings when adding keyboard shortcuts where appropriate.
Interaction tests verify first/last row jumps for both panels and existing panel-focus sequences; package and project checks pass.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Interaction tests verify row-jump endpoints in the exercises and sets panels, and confirm that ge and gs retain their focus behavior.
Help rendering exposes the Vim-style shortcuts and project instructions record the convention. GRACE graph and verification behavior matches the implementation.

Assumptions.Assumption: Existing Home and End shortcuts remain supported as aliases.
Vim-style preference applies when adding shortcuts and does not require retroactively replacing current bindings.
